items.text: Report on Recent San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Activities, Events and Announcements Dennis Herrera, SFPUC General Manager, provided comment regarding the United States Supreme Court ruling of City and County of San Francisco v. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency that was in favor of the City and County of San Francisco, and reiterated the Court held that the Clean Water Act allows EPA to issue water quality permits that contain limits only on a permit holder’s discharges which they can control, and not permits that make permit holders responsible for receiving water quality which they cannot control. SFPUC MARCH 11, 2025 MEETING MINUTES Page 2 of 8

items.title: Approve an increase of 283 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. WW-662R, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant Power Feed and Primary Switchgear Upgrades, with Blocka Construction, Inc.
items.text: Approve an increase of 283 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. WW-662R, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant Power Feed and Primary Switchgear Upgrades, with Blocka Construction, Inc., for a revised duration limit of 1,938 consecutive calendar days (approximately five years and four months), with no change to the contract amount, due to differing site conditions, design clarifications, delays in delivery of Hetch Hetchy Power to the Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant, operational constraints in the substation cut-over sequence, and construction of additional service protection equipment per Pacific Gas and Electric Company requirements

items.title: Approve Amendment No. 3 to Contract No. PRO.0092, Engineering Services for South Ocean Beach Coastal Erosion and Wastewater Infrastructure Protection, with Moffatt & Nichol-AGS Joint Venture, increasing the contract not
items.text: Approve Amendment No. 3 to Contract No. PRO.0092, Engineering Services for South Ocean Beach Coastal Erosion and Wastewater Infrastructure Protection, with Moffatt & Nichol-AGS Joint Venture, increasing the contract not-to-exceed amount by $7,000,000, and increasing the contract duration by six years, for a total not-to-exceed contract amount of $12,750,000 and a total contract duration of 15 years, to continue providing engineering design and support services for the Ocean Beach Climate Change Adaptation Project due to on-going extensive coordination efforts among multiple stakeholders, technical complexities, additional analysis and design efforts needed to address challenging negotiations between affected stakeholders, and significant delays associated with the California Coastal Commission, subject to Board of Supervisors approval under Charter Section 9.118.
